name: Erik Mesic

projects.name: Can’t Runoff: A Stakeholder Solution for the Environment
projects.description: A multi-stakeholder benefit-corporation solution addressing South Florida eutrophication.
projects.overview: A policy and strategy project proposing a multi-stakeholder benefit corporation to address South Florida eutrophication while aligning environmental and organizational incentives.
projects.role: Policy analysis, stakeholder strategy, and solution design.
details: Designed a multi-stakeholder benefit corporation solution for South Florida eutrophication.
Nominated for publication in The Call for Corporate Action: NYU Stern Student Voices, representing the top 1.6% of all NYU Stern student essays.

projects.name: Changing Social Landscapes: A Mixed-Method Examination
projects.description: Mixed-method research examining LLM bias through controlled sentiment-analysis conditions.
projects.overview: A mixed-method examination of changing social landscapes and LLM bias using controlled sentiment-analysis conditions and consultation with subject-matter experts.
projects.role: Research design, qualitative inquiry, quantitative analysis, and synthesis.
details: Conducted more than 1,600 sentiment analyses across 54 treatment conditions.
Consulted subject-matter experts at Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, Brown University, and the University of Chicago.
Combined qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine patterns of LLM bias.

projects.name: RAISE Act: Legislative Advocacy & Fiscal Modeling
projects.description: Legislative advocacy and fiscal modeling supporting proposed changes to Florida education funding and teacher compensation.
projects.overview: An ongoing legislative advocacy effort combining policy design, financial modeling, statutory drafting, and stakeholder outreach. It is presented under Experience as well as Projects because the work is both an active role and a substantive case study.
projects.role: Legislative advocate; policy modeling, statutory drafting, and stakeholder engagement.
details: Built financial models in Excel to analyze $600 million+ of state fund reallocations, applying synthetic conditional rate estimators to overcome data limitations.
Drafted statute restructuring advanced teacher compensation, with salary adjustments ranging from $20,000 to $320,000.
Secured bipartisan support and organizational lobbying from FIRST Robotics.

projects.name: Assessing Tucson Property
projects.description: Quantitative real-estate analysis combining financial modeling, market research, and MCMC simulation.
projects.overview: A detailed analysis of a Tucson single-family rental property and alternative management and investment strategies following a distressed situation.
projects.role: Investment analysis, financial modeling, market research, and scenario evaluation.
details: Produced a 40-page analysis of single-family rental options and vacancy scenarios.
Built quantitative models to evaluate returns and alternative strategies.
Assessed rental-property management options following a distressed situation.

researchInterests.title: LLM behavior, stability, and evaluation
researchInterests.description: Quantitative study of how model temperature and configuration affect output variation. A substantial planning effort reached the implementation stage, but the necessary computing access arrived late and the project may not proceed to completion; it is intentionally presented here as an open research interest rather than completed research.

researchInterests.title: South Florida environmental systems
researchInterests.description: Further ecological research on Lake Okeechobee, integrating existing research into an accessible, systems-level account of South Florida's environment and the relationships among water, agriculture, development, and eutrophication.

researchInterests.title: Legal questions surrounding generative AI
researchInterests.description: Research into the legal implications of LLMs, with particular attention to patent, copyright, and trademark infringement and the evolving boundaries of intellectual-property law.

researchInterests.title: The future of warfare and autonomous systems
researchInterests.description: Research interest in the future of war, especially the strategic, legal, ethical, and institutional implications of increasingly autonomous weapons and the possibility of fully autonomous warfare.
